LESSON: GRAFTING IN PLANTS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Production Techniques
Topic 4.1: Grafting in Plants

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grafting in Plants. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify parts of a plant (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit/seed)
2. explain what plants need to grow (water, air, light, soil)
3. describe how people in Kenya use plants for food, shade, or medicine
4. care for a seedling or garden plot safely

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAFTING IN PLANTS
Subject: AGRICULTURE · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grafting in Plants helps you succeed in AGRICULTURE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS ABOUT PLANTS
Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.
Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.
Without water and light, most seedlings wilt.

PART 1: Identify parts of a plant (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit/seed)

What this means
In this part you learn to identify parts of a plant (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit/seed). You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify parts of a plant (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit/seed).
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Grafting in Plants” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify parts of a plant (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit/seed). Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain what plants need to grow (water, air, light, soil)

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what plants need to grow (water, air, light, soil). You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what plants need to grow (water, air, light, soil).
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Grafting in Plants matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what plants need to grow (water, air, light, soil). Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Describe how people in Kenya use plants for food, shade, or medicine

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how people in Kenya use plants for food, shade, or medicine. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how people in Kenya use plants for food, shade, or medicine.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Grafting in Plants this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how people in Kenya use plants for food, shade, or medicine. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Care for a seedling or garden plot safely

What this means
In this part you learn to care for a seedling or garden plot safely. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: care for a seedling or garden plot safely.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Grafting in Plants” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can care for a seedling or garden plot safely. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grafting in Plants is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.

Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Grafting in Plants” around your school. (skill: identify parts of a plant (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit/seed))

Example 2: Say why Grafting in Plants matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: explain what plants need to grow (water, air, light, soil))

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Grafting in Plants this week. (skill: describe how people in Kenya use plants for food, shade, or medicine)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Grafting in Plants” around your school. (skill: care for a seedling or garden plot safely)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grafting in Plants to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify parts of a plant (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit/seed).
3. Practise this skill: explain what plants need to grow (water, air, light, soil).
4. Practise this skill: describe how people in Kenya use plants for food, shade, or medicine.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grafting in Plants from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grafting in Plants: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Grafting in Plants?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grafting in Plants means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify parts of a plant (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit/seed).
5. Be able to: explain what plants need to grow (water, air, light, soil).

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
